rows.title: Rest logistics create a recurring session bottleneck
rows.statement: Community evidence describes long rests as a sequence of GM-mediated identify, attune, copy-spell, watch, food, equipment, and recovery requests that can consume about an hour.

rows.title: Ordinary D&D players are directly affected by rest workflow
rows.statement: Every D&D5e table encounters short or long rests, and players either lose session time or skip meaningful downtime choices when the process is too manual.

rows.title: Rest automation must hand off to the authoritative system engine
rows.statement: Different tables choose different rest timing, food, exhaustion, downtime, recovery, and homebrew rules, so a product cannot assume one universal rest semantics.

rows.title: A portable rest artifact can describe workflow but not identical rules
rows.statement: Activities, approvals, costs, checks, and results can be represented neutrally, while resource recovery and system hooks require VTT/system adapters.

rows.title: Rest interest is not automatically payment intent
rows.statement: The presence of a recurring rest bottleneck establishes need, but a table may prefer skipping detail, using a free module, or changing house rules.

rows.title: Rest Recovery 5e covers the broad D&D5e recovery job
rows.statement: Rest Recovery 5e is current for Foundry 14 and covers class features, HP, partial recovery, exhaustion, food, water, starvation, and optional long-rest behavior.

rows.title: Ionrift Respite covers self-service rest and downtime
rows.statement: Ionrift Respite is current for Foundry 14 and provides player activities, GM-reviewed events, comfort, meals, recovery, short-rest flow, identify, attune, copy spell, custom event packs, and multiple system adapters.

rows.title: Stress Points & Rest occupies the survival-pressure variant
rows.statement: Stress Points & Rest adds stress, food, drink, comfort, medical supplies, environment checks, and purchases to the D&D5e rest loop.

rows.title: Character Builder already coordinates rest gating and compatibility
rows.statement: D&D5e Character Builder can manage GM-controlled rest availability and coordinates with Rest Recovery while handing authoritative rest execution back to D&D5e.

rows.title: Free module enthusiasm does not prove rest-product WTP
rows.statement: Ionrift community responses show strong appreciation for its free/non-commercial solution, but praise and sharing intent do not establish a non-zero price for a competing product.

rows.title: A generic rest engine is rejected
rows.statement: Rest Recovery 5e, Ionrift Respite, Stress Points & Rest, Character Builder, native system rests, and manual workflows occupy the broad rest surface.

rows.title: A rest event pack is also occupied
rows.statement: Ionrift already includes terrain-specific branching events and a custom event-pack schema, reducing differentiation for another generic camp-event product.

rows.title: Rest portability has a large adapter burden
rows.statement: Rest timing, resource recovery, exhaustion, item hooks, approvals, and system-specific activities differ across VTTs and game systems.

rows.title: Rest content remains a ruleset-specific possibility only
rows.statement: A qualified buyer might pay for a specific unresolved ruleset or event workflow, but the broad ordinary-table product case is closed until an exact failure survives the current stack.

rows.title: Rest and downtime are demoted as a product
rows.statement: Need is real but current free/current alternatives, compatibility burden, and absent product-specific WTP fail the selection gate.

rows.title: Large or unoptimized media can strand players
rows.statement: Community reports describe black screens, stalled loads, very long waits, and screen sharing when maps, videos, or assets are too large or incompatible.

rows.title: Foundry recommends asset formats and budgets
rows.statement: Foundry recommends WebP/OGG-style efficient formats, notes that scene media is distributed to connected users, and suggests keeping video maps near 50 MB when possible.

rows.title: Asset-heavy GMs have a recurring playability cost
rows.statement: GMs who buy or create map-heavy content, paid hosts, and campaign owners can lose session time or exclude a player when media fails.

rows.title: Compression alone is not playability proof
rows.statement: A smaller file can still fail because of pixel dimensions, codec, browser/GPU, missing path, disk, or network conditions.

rows.title: Playability Budget is a new conditional candidate
rows.statement: A local read-only scanner that estimates per-client risk and creates confirmed non-destructive variants may solve a different job from conversion.

rows.title: Geano Scene Optimizer already converts common media
rows.statement: Geano Scene Optimizer detects scene/audio formats, converts images to WebP and audio to OGG/Opus, preserves originals, and shows progress.

rows.title: DF Architect occupies flattening and scene-prep control
rows.statement: DF Architect provides tile flattening and map-prep features, but its package page reports an older verified Foundry release.

rows.title: Official guidance and free external tools are strong controls
rows.statement: Foundry's media/asset guides, Audacity, image converters, ffmpeg, core preload, hosting, and S3 can solve parts of the optimization job without a new module.

rows.title: The residual gap is verified playability and rollback
rows.statement: A differentiated product must report risk for declared clients, compare fidelity/audio behavior, preserve originals, and link every optimized copy to rollback.

rows.title: Generic media conversion is rejected
rows.statement: A converter that only reduces bytes will be displaced by current modules and free tools.

rows.title: Playability Budget targets a qualified GM payer
rows.statement: The buyer is an asset-heavy GM, paid host, or campaign owner with a named loading failure; small-map home tables are a negative control.

rows.title: Playability Budget can be local and non-destructive
rows.statement: The product can scan user-owned files, write optimized copies only after confirmation, preserve originals, and avoid live-world mutation.

rows.title: The portable artifact is an asset-risk manifest
rows.statement: A manifest can carry hashes, dimensions, codecs, budgets, checks, optimized variants, unsupported states, and rollback paths for manual use in another VTT.

rows.title: The eye-catching demo is weakest-client verification
rows.statement: A GM can see a large scene move from probable failure to verified under a low-bandwidth/low-GPU fixture while retaining the original.

rows.title: Playability Budget remains unselected pending payment and pilots
rows.statement: Qualified preference, a non-zero price, two pilots, and a home-table negative control are required before implementation.

rows.title: Current Media Optimizer occupies generic media conversion
rows.statement: Foundry currently lists a paid Media Optimizer that converts common image, audio, and video formats and can downscale images for Foundry 14.

rows.title: Black or gray scenes have multiple root causes
rows.statement: Foundry guidance identifies module conflicts, dimensions, hardware acceleration, missing paths, disk, and network as possible scene failures.

rows.title: Paid and organized-play GMs have a direct attendance cost
rows.statement: Paid sessions and organized-play events create a concrete consequence when a missing player forces cancellation or a refund.

rows.title: Premium side content is a real spending category
rows.statement: Ready-to-run side adventures and minimal-preparation content provide a payment anchor, although generic one-shots are crowded.

rows.title: Generic scheduling and live-session workspaces are occupied
rows.statement: Warhorn, SessionFlow, free one-shots, and the GM manual workflow cover parts of attendance response and session recovery.

rows.title: Table Rescue needs party-size recovery rather than generic content
rows.statement: The remaining hypothesis is a no-canon scenario with two-, three-, and five-player entry, late-join handling, safe rewards, and recap export.

rows.title: Media Safe Pack is demoted to a comparison arm
rows.statement: The current paid optimizer and official/free controls weaken a generic asset optimizer; only verified risk, fidelity, or rollback could reopen it.

rows.title: Table Rescue is conditional and unselected
rows.statement: The candidate has a clearer payer but still requires exact-alternative preference, non-zero price, two pilots, and repeat value.

rows.title: Table Rescue can export a neutral scenario receipt
rows.statement: A PDF plus neutral branch, reward, and recap manifest can travel without promising identical VTT runtime behavior.

rows.title: Publisher content must not be copied into a recovery product
rows.statement: The fixture and portable baseline must use original or licensed assets and avoid hosted account bridges or scraped content.

rows.title: No product was selected by Pass 164
rows.statement: The pass corrected the market ranking but did not establish product-specific willingness to pay.

rows.title: Injector v2 separates package, transport, reassembly, and adapter
rows.statement: The separation reduces coupling and makes the receiver small, testable, and reusable across application adapters.

rows.title: A package needs frame and whole-object digests
rows.statement: Manifest, frame hashes, and a final SHA-256 digest provide corruption and wrong-package detection.

rows.title: The receiver must accept duplicate and out-of-order frames
rows.statement: Resumable transport cannot assume ordered or exactly-once delivery.

rows.title: Incomplete transfers need resumable staging
rows.statement: IndexedDB can retain staged transfer state across refreshes, but the authoritative package remains the local packer output and final receipt.

rows.title: Base64 is encoding rather than compression
rows.statement: Base64 expands payloads, so compression must happen before framing and is not useful for already-compressed media.

rows.title: Workers can move package work off the UI thread
rows.statement: Compression, hashing, framing, and reassembly can run in a Worker to avoid freezing the Foundry UI.

rows.title: Adventure Documents bundle structured content with preserved links
rows.statement: Foundry Adventures can package multiple document types and provide a standard import path for structured content.

rows.title: Adventure media remains external
rows.statement: Media files are not embedded in an Adventure and require module or staged upload handling.

rows.title: Adventure re-import requires conflict and overwrite controls
rows.statement: The import plan can create or update content, so the receiver needs preview, target scope, base digest, backup, and explicit approval.

rows.title: Binary assets should remain outside scene JSON
rows.statement: Stable asset IDs and paths keep scene specifications small and permit deduplication and verified file staging.

rows.title: Base-digest patches can reduce repeated authoring payloads
rows.statement: A typed patch or constrained JSON Merge Patch can send only changes when the receiver confirms the expected base digest.

rows.title: The receiver should be a narrow Foundry adapter
rows.statement: The receiver should stage files, invoke supported upload/import APIs, and emit receipts rather than contain compilers or arbitrary script execution.

rows.title: The package format can be transport-agnostic
rows.statement: A neutral manifest and verified files can be consumed manually by another VTT even when runtime adapters differ.

rows.title: Existing DiceBox contracts reduce the first transport slice
rows.statement: Media registry, asset attestation, file browsing, receipts, and fixtures can be reused instead of rebuilt.

rows.title: The first receiver and audit slice is a 2â€“3 week effort
rows.statement: A focused Foundry v14 receiver plus read-only audit is estimated at 2â€“3 full-time weeks before variants, rollback UX, and cross-VTT work.

rows.title: Macro injection is not the primary product path
rows.statement: A short bootstrap may transport a package, but macro size, upload limits, memory, GPU, network, and import rules remain separate constraints.

rows.title: Foundry exposes startup lifecycle boundaries
rows.statement: The v14 API provides init, setup, and ready hooks that can anchor timing around module and world startup.

rows.title: Ready follows setup and setupGame initializes major runtime areas
rows.statement: The Game API describes setupGame as initializing Documents, UI applications, and Canvas before setup and ready completion.

rows.title: Module profile changes belong at a reload boundary
rows.statement: Foundry module activation and deactivation reload the world, so live silent mutation is unsafe as the first profile mechanism.

rows.title: User Timing and PerformanceObserver support custom receipts
rows.statement: Marks, measures, and observed entries can label Star*Tup phases without requiring DevTools operation.

rows.title: Resource timings can separate transfer from runtime work
rows.statement: Resource entries can help distinguish scripts, images, audio, video, and fetch transfer from later parsing or rendering.

rows.title: Long-task evidence has support limits
rows.statement: Long-task entries expose UI-thread work at or above 50 ms, but the API is not uniformly available and must report unsupported states.

rows.title: Chrome DevTools can visualize custom timing and GPU tracks
rows.statement: DevTools supports custom timing markers and main-thread, network, and GPU views, making it useful for fixture validation and expert diagnosis.

rows.title: Generic per-module blame is not reliable
rows.statement: A browser observer sees phases and script activity but cannot safely assign all third-party work to a module without controlled A/B runs or exact adapters.

rows.title: Startup Budget should measure first usable map
rows.statement: The useful outcome is navigation to world ready, first usable UI, scene activation, and first interactive map rather than a single aggregate load number.

rows.title: Profiles must preserve a module/settings snapshot
rows.statement: Dependency-aware profile changes need a before state, explicit delta, reload boundary, and verified restore result.

rows.title: DiceBox media registry and attestation fit Star*Tup
rows.statement: Existing local code can supply stable IDs, hashes, dimensions, variants, and read-only verification for the asset portion.

rows.title: Workers and hashed storage reduce UI and stale-cache risk
rows.statement: Hashing, compression, and manifest processing should run in Workers; staged cache keys should include content and target/profile identity.

rows.title: Startup Budget is the first Star*Tup technical slice
rows.statement: A read-only profiler with reversible suggestions is safer and more decision-useful than arbitrary third-party lazy loading or direct world edits.

rows.title: Foundry already supports scene preload
rows.statement: A scene can request connected users to load its image and video assets in the background before activation.

rows.title: Foundry recommends role-appropriate media formats
rows.statement: Official guidance recommends WebP for images, WebM for many videos, and OGG for audio while warning that client CPU work can increase.

rows.title: Byte reduction does not equal faster playability
rows.statement: A smaller asset can still decode slowly, exceed GPU budgets, reduce fidelity, or fail on a client.

rows.title: Star*Tup should use content-addressed derivatives
rows.statement: A source hash, dimensions, codec, role, target profile, derivative settings, and rollback link can identify a safe variant without overwriting the source.

rows.title: Preload should be bounded and policy-driven
rows.statement: The optimizer should choose the next likely scene or declared session bundle, cap concurrency, and stop at client budget limits.

rows.title: Browser asset storage is best-effort and evictable
rows.statement: IndexedDB and CacheStorage can be cleared or evicted, so cache entries must be revalidated and never serve as the sole authority.

rows.title: Cache identity must include content and target context
rows.statement: Hash, Foundry/system/world, scene role, client profile, and derivative settings are needed to reject stale variants.

rows.title: Workers can analyze and resize images off the UI thread
rows.statement: createImageBitmap is available in workers with resize options in supported browsers, allowing bounded analysis without blocking input.

rows.title: Unsupported formats and storage failures need explicit receipts
rows.statement: A fallback or unsupported state is safer than silently publishing a derivative or waiting forever for preload.

rows.title: The asset wedge is verified selection and recovery
rows.statement: A generic converter or preload toggle is occupied; Star*Tup must prove a declared client became usable earlier without fidelity or rollback loss.

rows.title: Foundry has client, user, and world setting scopes
rows.statement: Client settings are device/browser-specific, User settings are per user in a world, and World settings apply to all users and clients.

rows.title: Module activation is GM-controlled and reloads the world
rows.statement: Saving module activation changes requires appropriate permission and reloads the world with the selected modules.

rows.title: A performance profile cannot be one global switch
rows.statement: Client rendering and asset choices differ from shared world/module choices and require different authority.

rows.title: Foundry snapshots do not include every external media asset
rows.statement: Package snapshots store package data but may omit assets outside the module/world/system folders.

rows.title: Asset moves can break restored links
rows.statement: Restoring older world data does not automatically restore media moved to a different relative path.

rows.title: Star*Tup needs separate client and world profile artifacts
rows.statement: ClientProfile can carry local settings and asset budgets; WorldProfile can carry module activation, dependencies, and shared settings.

rows.title: Profile changes need immutable snapshots and explicit diffs
rows.statement: Before state, requested delta, observed state, and rollback result make a profile change auditable.

rows.title: A stale base must stop profile application
rows.statement: Changed Foundry, system, module, world, settings, or asset identity invalidates a previously prepared profile.

rows.title: Cross-VTT portability belongs at the receipt layer
rows.statement: Profile concepts can be neutral, but applying settings and module dependencies remains adapter-specific.

rows.title: Foundry modules have a versioned manifest and dependency surface
rows.statement: A module manifest can declare compatibility, scripts, styles, packs, relationships, and optional socket capability.

rows.title: Owlbear extensions can store namespaced scene and player metadata
rows.statement: Owlbear metadata is shared with other extensions and should use a namespaced key convention.

rows.title: Owlbear exposes an extension asset upload surface
rows.statement: An extension can upload images into the current user's storage, providing a narrow asset adapter path.

rows.title: Roll20 Mod Scripts are a separate sandboxed API
rows.statement: Roll20 provides scripts, events, objects, chat, and utilities through its own Mod Scripts surface rather than Foundry module APIs.

rows.title: Portable Star*Tup records should be evidence contracts
rows.statement: Asset manifests, profile intents, timing receipts, rollback receipts, capability reports, and unsupported states can cross VTT boundaries.

rows.title: Runtime optimization remains adapter-specific
rows.statement: Module lifecycle, filesystem access, asset storage, permission, and profile application differ by VTT.

rows.title: One core worker and schema package can reduce creation time
rows.statement: Hashing, receipt, manifest, and fixture logic can be shared while small adapters translate platform actions.

rows.title: Adapters must preserve unknown and refused fields
rows.statement: A receiving VTT must not discard information it cannot implement or silently claim parity.

rows.title: Foundry is the only initial runtime target
rows.statement: A second VTT should begin as a read-only import/receipt fixture after Foundry evidence exists.

rows.title: Star*Tup M0â€“M2 exists as a standalone package
rows.statement: The Windows-safe startuptup package contains benchmark, Foundry lifecycle, profile, and rollback contracts without external runtime dependencies.

rows.title: Benchmark receipts cover six user-visible milestones
rows.statement: The local receipt contract records navigation, world-ready, UI-ready, scene-active, map-usable, and first-input stages.

rows.title: Profile contracts separate client and world scope
rows.statement: Explicit ClientProfile and WorldProfile constructors keep local player settings separate from GM-controlled shared module state.

rows.title: M0â€“M2 pure tests pass
rows.statement: The standalone package passes 8/8 Node tests and syntax checks; tests cover ordered milestones, dependency diffs, explicit profile scopes, stale-base rejection, rollback, and fake Foundry hooks.

rows.title: Live Foundry integration remains blocked
rows.statement: The current slice does not apply profiles, edit worlds, upload assets, rewrite modules, or control a browser; exact runtime evidence is still required.

rows.title: The next Star*Tup gate is an exact disposable Foundry fixture
rows.statement: A Foundry v14.367 GM/player fixture must produce runtime lifecycle and map-usability evidence before live integration is considered.

rows.title: Star*Tup has a deterministic disposable fixture contract
rows.statement: Fixture plans bind a caller-supplied ID, exact target metadata, GM/Player3 contexts, ordered lifecycle stages, and explicit no-write/no-raw-data flags without generating nondeterministic identity.

rows.title: Fixture observations are redacted by contract
rows.statement: Star*Tup fixture observations record stages, resource counts, long-task counts, unsupported labels, and notes while rejecting raw Foundry IDs, documents, module payloads, and asset bytes.

rows.title: Incomplete fixture evidence stays blocked
rows.statement: A missing client context, missing lifecycle stage, or explicitly blocked observation prevents an observed receipt while preserving no-write guarantees.

rows.title: Star*Tup M0â€“M2 verification passes eight tests
rows.statement: The standalone package passes eight Node tests, including deterministic fixture observed and blocked cases and explicit client/world profile scope, plus syntax checks.

rows.title: DiceBox compatibility is documented without importing the dirty checkout
rows.statement: Star*Tup preserves receipt and fixture vocabulary while keeping the standalone package dependency-free; the existing media, attestation, and FilePicker contracts remain reserved for later slices.

rows.title: Asset and file adapters remain deferred
rows.statement: M0â€“M2 do not browse Foundry files, attest bytes, replace media, or claim preload improvement; those surfaces remain a later M3 gate.

rows.title: Fishing Minigame uses biome-specific fish pools
rows.statement: The Fishing Minigame supports different fish by biome, and Underdark is one of the supported fishing biomes.

rows.title: Fish use five rarity bands
rows.statement: Fishing Minigame fish rarities are Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare, and Legendary.

rows.title: Fishing ponds use three tiers
rows.statement: Fishing regions are assigned one of three pond tiers: Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3.

rows.title: Tier 1 fishing rarity profile
rows.statement: Tier 1 ponds contain Common and Uncommon fish with an occasional Rare fish; no exact percentage split is canon yet.

rows.title: Tier 2 fishing rarity profile
rows.statement: Tier 2 ponds make Rare fish more common than Tier 1 and add Very Rare fish; no exact percentage split is canon yet.

rows.title: Tier 3 fishing rarity profile
rows.statement: Tier 3 ponds can produce all five fish rarities and have a 5 percent chance of hooking a Legendary fish.

rows.title: Fishing Minigame is Region-driven
rows.statement: The Fishing Minigame is attached to Foundry Regions, and fishing Regions are placed over the bodies of water where players can fish.

rows.title: Blingdenstone gathering maps must integrate fishing Regions
rows.statement: Any surrounding Blingdenstone hunter/gatherer map that contains fishable water must plan and place Fishing Minigame Regions over those water bodies with the Underdark biome and an intentional pond tier.

rows.title: Mining deposits are visible Region interactions
rows.statement: Hunter/gatherer maps may show visible ore artwork with an invisible configured Foundry Region over the deposit; players click the deposit from Token Controls to mine it.

rows.title: Mining requires a pickaxe
rows.statement: An actor must possess a qualifying mining pick or pickaxe in inventory before an extraction attempt can begin.

rows.title: Ore veins have five extraction attempts
rows.statement: Each configured ore vein provides five extraction attempts before the vein is depleted.

rows.title: Mining mutation is GM-authoritative
rows.statement: For multiplayer extraction, the active GM validates actor ownership, pickaxe presence, Region configuration, remaining attempts, computes yield from the reported native Athletics total, advances shared vein depletion, and awards ore.

rows.title: Mining failure is fail-closed
rows.statement: If no active GM can resolve a protected mutation, actor ownership is invalid, the pickaxe is missing, or the vein is depleted, the mining routine awards nothing and does not advance a swing.

rows.title: Mining Regions must coexist with fishing Regions
rows.statement: The mining interaction layer must preserve native Region editing and coexist with the installed regionwright-fishing Region click behavior rather than replacing or swallowing it.

rows.title: Mining deposits expose a reset path
rows.statement: A GM-only reset operation must restore a configured deposit to zero attempts used for future gathering-map refresh workflows.

rows.title: Blingdenstone Underdark 15-map live roster
rows.statement: The live world the-forgotten-realms contains the intended 15 Blingdenstone/Underdark exploration Scenes with stable mapIds. Current Scene IDs are recorded in BLINGDENSTONE_UNDERDARK_LIVE_STATE_2026-10-03.md.

rows.title: Underdark Region population
rows.statement: The 15 live exploration Scenes currently contain 278 Regions and 252 embedded RegionBehaviors. A prior dedicated level diagnostic found zero wrong-Level Region assignments; interaction defects are not explained by Scene Level placement.

rows.title: Underdark environment live settings
rows.statement: All 15 exploration Scenes currently use tokenVision=false, fog.mode=0, darknessLevel=0.84, darknessLock=true, cycle=false, and globalLight.enabled=false.

rows.title: Twenty-four live fishing Regions
rows.statement: The 15 exploration Scenes contain 24 Regionwright Fishing Regions. All 24 currently use Region visibility ALWAYS with default player OBSERVER ownership, matching the module invisible-hitbox design that renders clickable fishing Regions at alpha 0.001.

rows.title: Twenty-four live mining Regions with partial clickability repair
rows.statement: The 15 exploration Scenes contain 24 Regionwright Mining Regions configured under flags.regionwright-mining.miningDeposit. All 24 currently give players Observer ownership but remain GAMEMASTER visibility, so mining clickability is not yet certified as repaired.

rows.title: Underdark teleport network verified
rows.statement: The approved network has 15 bidirectional links / 30 directed teleports across Northwest, Northeast, West Waterway, and East branches; the completed verification receipt reported all 30 directions PASS.

rows.title: Southeast and Southern hub routes remain unresolved
rows.statement: The hub Southeast pair exists but no matching destination exists in the current 15-map network; Southern is also unresolved. No destination may be guessed. The East manual pair must be preserved unless explicitly migrated.

rows.title: Blingdenstone Exploration Items inventory
rows.statement: The Blingdenstone Exploration Items folder diagnostic mapped 127 loot Items across five child folders plus root; all initially used the generic D&D5e loot SVG and stable flags.world.diceboxExploration metadata is available for canonical targeting.

rows.title: Exploration item name targeting is unsafe
rows.statement: Washed-Up Expedition Debris exists as two distinct exploration Items, so selectors and interaction wiring must target flags.world.diceboxExploration.itemId before display name.

rows.title: Blingdenstone gathering vendor allocation
rows.statement: The campaign uses ten specialized Blingdenstone gathering vendors with non-overlapping category ownership: Melli forage; Brannik fishing catches excluding pearls; Durnik ore/metals; Nimri gems/pearls/crystals; Velka fossils/specimens; Zibbin reagents; Bod salvage; Korrin specialist mining/survey equipment; Talla textiles; Orvin lore and puzzle-fragment research without consuming fragments.

rows.title: Blingdenstone long-rest resource census
rows.statement: The full Blingdenstone long-rest reset reported 24 mining nodes reset, 24 fishing spots ready, and exploration reset, consistent with the live Region census.

rows.title: General exploration Region interaction gap
rows.statement: Many non-fishing/non-mining exploration Regions still require explicit interaction behavior. Missing interaction behavior is a separate problem from Scene Level assignment and must be solved using stable exploration IDs without duplicating fishing/mining mechanical ownership.

rows.title: The 15-map gathering network plus Outer Travel Hub has exact live Scene bindings
rows.statement: The campaign uses 15 named Underdark exploration Scenes plus Blingdenstone â€” Outer Travel Hub; the complete Scene UUID roster is recorded in docs/BLINGDENSTONE-GATHERING-RUNTIME-2026-10-03.json and is the current binding authority for this campaign slice.

rows.title: Gathering network current Region inventory includes the hub

The earlier 278/252 counts in SRC-BLINGDENSTONE-LIVE-174 covered only the 15 exploration maps and remain compatible.

rows.title: Exploration Item catalog is live with 127 Items and 146 mappings
rows.statement: The live world contains 127 Items flagged world.diceboxExploration mapped across 146 source Region references: 32 renewable, 28 salvage, 42 discovery, 10 puzzle, and 15 creature Items. Reset-policy counts are 32 per-character-long-rest, 80 global-one-time, and 15 encounter-dependent.

rows.statement: Macro.wmagIrvqTCZoLpRk (Dicebox â€” Exploration Discovery v2) has default LIMITED ownership and is referenced by 177 exploration-runtime Region behaviors. The runtime uses passive Perception, private player UI, self-roll Investigation, and active-GM authoritative award/state mutation.

rows.title: Exploration Discovery v2 has exact-world execution evidence
rows.statement: Four Actors currently carry Dicebox exploration-v2 runtime state with observed signal statuses including perception-fail, investigation-fail, success, cancelled, and locked plus collected/used timestamps. This proves the runtime executed in the exact world but does not certify every multiplayer privacy or reconnect edge case.

rows.title: Blingdenstone network has 24 configured fishing spots
rows.statement: The exact world contains 24 Regionwright Fishing spots across 10 exploration Scenes. Tier distribution is 10 common, 12 uncommon, and 2 rare; configured spots use Glowworms, visibility ALWAYS, hidden=false, and default Observer permission for player interaction.

rows.title: Installed fishing has no persistent pond-depletion reset state
rows.statement: The installed fishing implementation persists spot configuration and inventory mutations but no pond-depletion, catch-count, or long-rest cooldown state. Long-rest handling therefore verifies fishing Region readiness rather than restoring caught fish or consumed bait.

rows.title: Blingdenstone network has 24 configured mining deposits
rows.statement: The exact world contains 24 Regionwright Mining deposits: 9 iron, 8 silver, 4 copper, and 3 gold. Five deposits were fully depleted at the later snapshot, providing live evidence that shared five-swing depletion state has been exercised during play.

rows.title: Mining invisible-clickable document repair is now applied
rows.statement: All 24 configured mining Regions in the later snapshot are hidden=false, visibility=GAMEMASTER, locked=false, and default ownership=OBSERVER. This supersedes the earlier partial-repair observation; controlled non-GM click certification remains tracked separately.

rows.title: Five manually drawn Regions were added as mining nodes without geometry changes
rows.statement: Steamstone Pools Regions 7Bx0X2VRr4J9dn5u and uXC3QIVJSAwJufFu are copper and silver; Forgotten Waystation QTa9aePxyoDuRsEU is gold; Shellwater Basin cfKOGcJg5JSohOAB and 8Y4q8DU4HwGYrPNV are iron and copper. Their supplied Region geometry is authoritative and was preserved.

rows.title: Installed mining module is newer than the project output copy
rows.statement: The installed regionwright-mining manifest is v0.1.4 with socket=true, while outputs/regionwright-mining/module.json is still v0.1.0 with socket=true. The installed runtime and project source copy are divergent and must be reconciled before the successful live fixes are considered durable source.

rows.title: Private mining swing patch is present but awaits restart certification
rows.statement: Installed regionwright-mining v0.1.4 contains a selfroll Athletics call and whispers the mining summary to the triggering client. Static syntax/source checks pass, but this privacy change still requires a Foundry restart and non-GM player test before full-function certification.

rows.title: Blingdenstone long-rest reset preserves earned inventory
rows.statement: The accepted long-rest contract clears Dicebox exploration actor and Region runtime/claim state, resets all configured mining deposits through the mining API, and verifies fishing Region readiness while preserving awarded exploration Items, caught fish, consumed bait, Region shapes, teleports, and map geometry. A prior live reset reported 24 mining nodes reset, 24 fishing spots ready, and exploration reset.

rows.title: Functional Regions must not use Foundry hidden=true for player invisibility
rows.statement: In Foundry v14 a hidden Region deactivates its RegionBehaviors. Functional player-invisible Regions therefore remain hidden=false and use Region visibility/ownership or module-level near-transparent rendering; mining additionally requires Observer permission and an unlocked Region for click handling.

rows.title: Mining uses native Athletics
rows.statement: Superseded: the original implementation used a D&D5e Strength (Athletics) check to determine extracted quantity; this gameplay rule is superseded by F-856.

rows.title: Mining uses a three-strike timing puzzle
rows.statement: One extraction attempt contains three pulsing-circle timing strikes with full-cycle targets of 1500 ms, 1350 ms, and 1200 ms. Each strike scores 0-5 from nested accuracy bands, and rounded average score determines 0-5 ore units.

rows.title: Timing puzzle preserves one-attempt depletion semantics
rows.statement: Completing all three timing strikes consumes exactly one shared vein attempt. Cancellation before completion or fail-closed rejection consumes no attempt.

rows.title: GM computes timing yield from validated scores
rows.statement: The active GM validates ownership, pickaxe, Region state, and exactly three integer strike scores in the range 0-5, computes the rounded average yield, then performs serialized depletion and ore award mutation.

rows.title: Regionwright Mining v0.2.0 timing source passes local validation
rows.statement: Durable project source now contains the three-stage timing resolver/UI at v0.2.0. Pure timing/state tests pass and node syntax checks pass for mining-engine.js, catalog.js, mining.js, and module.js; live Foundry behavior is not yet certified.

rows.title: Regionwright Mining v0.2.0 is installed and served by the exact Foundry runtime
rows.statement: The installed seven changed files match durable source byte-for-byte. Foundry 14.367 relaunched regionwright-testmap on port 30000 and HTTP reads returned module version 0.2.0 with socket=true plus the new timing UI/engine code; player gameplay remains uncertified.

rows.title: Mining exposes a no-write GM timing test
rows.statement: Region Controls should expose a GM-only Test Mining Minigame tool adjacent to Fishing Ponds. The test runs the real three-stage timing UI but performs no inventory, Region, attempt, or socket mutation.

rows.title: Regionwright Mining v0.2.1 serves GM-selectable remote timing tests
rows.statement: The GM Region Controls palette now has a bullseye Test Mining Minigame tool ordered after Fishing Ponds and before Mining Deposits. Its dialog lists all active users; the selected user receives the real three-stage timing UI over the module socket. Test mode bypasses pickaxe checks and performs no reward, Region update, depletion, or attempt consumption.

rows.title: Mining timing UI shows graded live accuracy feedback
rows.statement: The timing ring and arena should visibly intensify as current timing quality improves, with the 5/5 zone receiving the strongest bright-green treatment.

rows.title: Regionwright Mining v0.2.2 serves graded timing and perfect-hit feedback
rows.statement: Foundry serves v0.2.2 with live score-zone tinting on the pulsing ring/arena, per-strike result callouts, and an exceptional 5/5 PERFECT bright-green flash. Syntax/unit tests pass and deployed files match durable source.

rows.title: Perfect mining hit requires the tiny center bullseye
rows.statement: Only normalized timing radius <= 0.025 scores 5/5 Perfect. The visible Perfect ring is reduced to 38 px around the center bullseye, while the surrounding precision area scores Excellent or lower.

rows.title: Mining timing score derives from rendered ring diameter
rows.statement: The timing ring renders from 250 px down to 20 px. Strike score is determined from rendered diameter: <=26 Perfect, <=62 Excellent, <=103 Great, <=149 Good, <=200 Glancing, and >200 Miss.

rows.title: Regionwright Mining v0.2.4 serves reachable diameter-based Perfect timing
rows.statement: The installed module matches durable source, Foundry serves v0.2.4, the ring minimum scale is 0.08 (20 px from a 250 px base), Perfect is <=26 px, and the UI uses rendered diameter for both live score feedback and strike resolution.

rows.title: Current mining expansion is ore-only
rows.statement: Immediate mining catalogue work is limited to Copper, Tin, Iron, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Mithral, Arandur, and Hizagkuur as raw metallic ore/deposit candidates.

rows.title: Refined and special resources are deferred
rows.statement: Deferred refined/alloy materials: Adamantine, Darksteel, Telstang/Truesilver, Dlarun/Icesteel, Titansteel/Relic Iron, and Baatorian Green Steel. Deferred special-resource nodes: Fever Iron, Chardalyn, Star Metal/Starfall Ore, and Solanian Truesteel.

rows.title: Ore uses fixed per-unit prices
rows.statement: Each ore type has one fixed sale price per 1 lb unit. Mining value does not roll per item or by vein quality; the existing 0-5 yield from timing performance provides the quantity variance.

rows.title: Rare ore economy research suggests 5:1 ore-to-ingot abstraction
rows.statement: A provisional crafting abstraction of 5 one-pound ore units per refined ingot pairs cleanly with the existing 0-5 mining yield and discrete weapon/armor ingot recipes. Proposed values are Mithral 100 gp/ore, Arandur 1,000 gp/ore, and Hizagkuur 625 gp/ore; these are not locked pending user approval.

rows.title: Mining timing difficulty scales by ore
rows.statement: Common Copper/Tin/Iron use 1500/1350/1200 ms; Silver 1400/1250/1100; Gold 1300/1150/1000; Platinum 1200/1050/900; Mithral 1100/950/825; Hizagkuur 1000/875/800; Arandur 950/850/800. Score geometry and 0-5 yield remain unchanged.

rows.title: Nine-ore fixed price catalogue
rows.statement: Mineable ore prices are Iron 1 sp, Tin 3 sp, Copper 5 sp, Silver 2 gp, Gold 10 gp, Platinum 25 gp, Mithral 100 gp, Hizagkuur 625 gp, and Arandur 1,000 gp per one-pound unit. Adamantine is excluded from the mineable catalogue.

rows.title: Mining and Fishing share a Gathering HUD
rows.statement: The Regionwright fishing HUD will become a tabbed Regionwright Gathering HUD. Fishing preserves its current setup/test surface; Mining adds ore configuration and all-ore player testing through the Mining module public API.

rows.title: Mining v0.3.0 serves nine ore difficulties and shared Gathering HUD integration
rows.statement: Foundry serves Regionwright Mining v0.3.0 and Regionwright Fishing v0.1.16. Mining contains nine mineable resources, seven ore timing profiles, ore-selectable local/remote no-write tests, and its Region control opens the shared Mining HUD tab. Fishing provides a tabbed Regionwright Gathering HUD with Fishing and Mining setup/test surfaces through the Mining public API.

rows.title: High-tier ore timing profiles are faster
rows.statement: Very Rare Platinum uses 1100/950/800 ms; Exceptional Mithral 950/800/675; Legendary Hizagkuur 825/700/600; Legendary+ Arandur 750/625/525. Common through Rare retain their existing timing profiles and score geometry.

rows.title: Mining v0.3.1 serves accelerated high-tier timing
rows.statement: Foundry serves v0.3.1 with Platinum 1100/950/800 ms, Mithral 950/800/675, Hizagkuur 825/700/600, and Arandur 750/625/525. Common through Gold are unchanged.

rows.title: High-tier ores use progressively tighter scoring geometry
rows.statement: Copper, Tin, Iron, and Silver retain score thresholds 26/62/103/149/200 px. Gold uses 25/56/92/132/175; Platinum 24/52/84/120/160; Mithral 23/48/76/108/145; Hizagkuur 22/44/70/98/132; Arandur 22/40/64/90/120. Thresholds are maximum rendered diameters for scores 5 through 1; larger rings score 0.

rows.title: Mining v0.3.2 serves tighter Gold-and-higher success zones
rows.statement: Foundry serves v0.3.2 with Gold thresholds 25/56/92/132/175 px, Platinum 24/52/84/120/160, Mithral 23/48/76/108/145, Hizagkuur 22/44/70/98/132, and Arandur 22/40/64/90/120 for scores 5 through 1. The visible target rings shrink with those profiles and rings beyond the score-1 boundary miss.

rows.title: Mining pulse accelerates near the center
rows.statement: The moving mining ring uses q = r + 0.30*r*(1-r), where r is the original linear pulse ratio. Endpoints and each ore full-cycle duration are preserved; instantaneous motion is about 30% faster at the center and slower near the outside. Score geometry remains unchanged.

rows.title: Mining v0.3.3 serves deterministic center acceleration
rows.statement: Foundry serves v0.3.3 with TIMING_CENTER_ACCELERATION 0.30 and q = r + 0.30*r*(1-r). Mining runtime applies the transform each animation frame before rendering/scoring. Full pulse duration, endpoints, ore speed profiles, and ore-specific score zones are unchanged.

rows.title: Hunting & Gathering is a standalone Regionwright module
rows.statement: Regionwright: Hunting & Gathering will own Hunting, Fishing, Mining, and Gathering as one environmental-resource product. Existing Fishing and Mining remain authoritative during scaffold/migration.

rows.title: Hunting & Gathering uses a compact GM mini-HUD
rows.statement: The new module uses a compact active-GM DialogV2 HUD modeled on the Puzzle HUD. It owns orchestration only: activity tabs, selected Region context, setup/clear actions, and test targeting; subsystem catalogs/gameplay remain in their APIs until migrated.

rows.title: Hunting & Gathering v0.1.0 scaffold is built but not live
rows.statement: The Region Editor source and dist contain regionwright-hunting-gathering v0.1.0 with a compact four-tab GM HUD. Fishing and Mining setup/test controls delegate through their public APIs; Hunting and Gathering display explicit planned states. The package has not been cut over or enabled in the live Foundry world, and legacy controls remain untouched.

rows.title: H&G scaffold passes full Regionwright regression
rows.statement: The H&G scaffold plus Fishing API bridge passes 251 of 251 Regionwright tests, and source/dist hashes match for the new H&G module and Fishing v0.1.17 build.

rows.title: Hunting v0.1 core loop
rows.statement: Hunting uses visible D&D5e Survival to determine quarry quality, visible Stealth to determine real shot distance and target scale, a mouse/draw/release bow minigame driven by draw strength + distance + gravity + wind + aim sway, and visible Survival to harvest after a lethal shot.

rows.title: Hunting requires a dedicated Hunting Bow
rows.statement: Real Hunting accepts only the Regionwright Hunting Bow identified by the module huntingBow flag. Generic bows and name matching do not satisfy the equipment gate. Test mode is exempt.

rows.title: Hunting v0.2.0 prototype is built
rows.statement: Regionwright: Hunting & Gathering v0.2.0 contains visible Survival tracking, visible Stealth range selection, a mouse-aimed hold-to-draw/release shooting prototype with draw strength, real distance, gravity, crosswind, deterministic live sway/fatigue, deer hit zones, and visible Survival harvesting. Real hunts require the exact flagged Hunting Bow; test hunts bypass equipment and rewards.

rows.title: Hunting v0.2.0 passes source validation
rows.statement: The Hunting v0.2.0 addition passes 261 of 261 Regionwright tests, all relevant syntax checks, and source/dist hash agreement for module.js, module.json, README.md, hunting-engine.js, hunting.js, and hunting-gathering.css.

rows.title: H&G v0.2.0 is installed and served on the test world host
rows.statement: The v0.2.0 distribution was copied to Foundry Data/modules/regionwright-hunting-gathering with all 7 files hash-matching source. The exact regionwright-testmap world was restarted and serves v0.2.0 module.json and hunting.js over port 30000.

rows.title: H&G is not yet enabled in regionwright-testmap
rows.statement: Inspection of core.moduleConfiguration after the restart shows regionwright-fishing=true and regionwright-mining=true, but no regionwright-hunting-gathering entry. Therefore the new H&G runtime and Hunting Bow installer have not yet executed in-world.

rows.title: Regionwright uses a Foundry-like flat window language
rows.statement: Regionwright UI should use the Foundry application window as the primary visual surface, with translucent charcoal gray content, neutral text, subtle dividers, and no decorative nested card panels for routine sections. Borders are reserved for functional interactive elements such as game canvases, controls, tabs, and buttons.

rows.title: H&G v0.2.1 implements the flat Regionwright UI language
rows.statement: Hunting & Gathering v0.2.1 removes decorative card styling from the HUD and Hunting header/stages, uses a translucent charcoal Foundry-like content surface, subtle divider lines, and keeps functional borders on controls and the shooting arena.

rows.title: H&G v0.2.1 validation and deployment completed
rows.statement: The UI refresh passes 262/262 Regionwright tests, source/dist hashes match, installed files match the build, Foundry restarted regionwright-testmap as PID 26672, and HTTP serves v0.2.1 with the flat charcoal CSS rules.

rows.title: Regionwright inherits native Foundry UI styling
rows.statement: Regionwright dialogs should rely on Foundry DialogV2/application chrome, standard-form conventions, native buttons/selects/checkboxes/focus states, and Foundry application variables. Custom CSS is limited to layout and game-specific visualizations.

rows.title: H&G v0.2.2 uses native Foundry UI primitives
rows.statement: Hunting & Gathering v0.2.2 uses Foundry standard-form and nav.tabs conventions, leaves DialogV2 window surfaces and native controls to Foundry, and limits Regionwright CSS to layout, native-variable-based hierarchy, and the Hunting game canvas.

rows.title: H&G v0.2.2 validation and deployment passed
rows.statement: The native UI conversion passes 262/262 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed-file hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap restarted successfully as PID 30772 serving v0.2.2.

rows.title: Hunting separates roll and shooting windows
rows.statement: Tracking, Approach, and Harvest use compact player-facing roll windows while bow aiming/shooting runs in a separate Hunt window. Skill buttons immediately roll with no D&D5e configuration popup.

rows.title: Hunting skill checks are normal-only
rows.statement: Module-owned Hunting Survival and Stealth checks force D20 NORMAL mode and suppress the D&D5e roll configuration dialog while preserving the Actor current skill calculation.

rows.title: Hunting shot display uses a practical sight zero and resize-stable markers
rows.statement: The dedicated Hunting Bow uses a practical sight-zero launch angle so ordinary full-draw shots are not modeled as perfectly horizontal. Quarry artwork is visible on initial render, Show Hitboxes only overlays anatomy, and fired aim/impact markers are target-local so resizing cannot separate them from the quarry.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.0 live-play corrections are built and served
rows.statement: Regionwright Hunting v0.3.0 separates Track/Approach and Harvest rolls from the dedicated shooting window, suppresses D&D5e roll configuration and forces NORMAL d20 mode, paints the quarry on initial render, uses a 30-yard Hunting Bow sight zero, and anchors resolved aim/impact markers to the target.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.0 validation passed
rows.statement: The v0.3.0 correction passes 267/267 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and Foundry serves v0.3.0 from the exact regionwright-testmap runtime on port 30000.

rows.title: Hunting uses RK4 source-backed arrow ballistics
rows.statement: Hunting v0.3.1 numerically integrates arrow flight with fourth-order Runge-Kutta, earth gravity, air-relative quadratic drag using kappa 0.00231 m^-1, 74.5 m/s full-draw reference velocity, and 7 cm sight height.

rows.title: Hunting uses practical multi-distance sight references
rows.statement: The Hunting Bow uses 20, 30, 40, 50, and 60 yard sight references and selects the closest lower pin for the known shot range. At 65 yd a full-draw calm shot using the 60 yd pin is about 0.28 m low rather than the prior 1.66 m.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.1 source validation passed
rows.statement: The RK4 ballistics revision passes 268 of 268 Regionwright tests and source/dist hash agreement.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.2 draw playtest keeps strength continuous
rows.statement: The draw playtest uses 1.5 seconds to full draw with 50/75/100 milestone pulses and a temporary four-stage bow visual, but shot power remains the exact continuous release strength rather than discrete quality tiers.

rows.title: Hunting full draw gets a short settled window before fatigue
rows.statement: The v0.3.2 playtest targets about 0.7 seconds of stable full draw after reaching 100%, then progressively increases sway from fatigue.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.2 draw-feel playtest is live
rows.statement: The v0.3.2 playtest uses a 1.5-second continuous draw, 50/75/100 one-shot milestone pulses, a temporary four-stage bow visual, a 0.7-second settled full-draw window, and preserves continuous RK4 shot strength.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.2 validation passed
rows.statement: The draw-feel playtest passes 269/269 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and Foundry serves v0.3.2 from regionwright-testmap on port 30000.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.2 draw-feedback experiment was rejected
rows.statement: Live play rejected the v0.3.2 whole-draw slowdown, milestone-pulse feedback, temporary four-stage bow visual, and settled-window experiment. Those behaviors are removed in v0.3.3.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.3 uses nonlinear draw tension
rows.statement: Hunting v0.3.3 uses a 1.3-second quadratic ease-out draw curve so early pull is fast and progress slows substantially near 100%, while release strength remains continuous and feeds RK4 ballistics.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.4 restores draw-marker pulses
rows.statement: The 50%, 75%, and 100% one-shot draw-marker pulses return because live play found them useful. The rejected four-stage placeholder bow art remains removed, and markers do not create discrete shot-quality tiers.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.4 uses increasing-force heavy-bow draw progression
rows.statement: Draw progression is modeled as constant player pulling power against a non-compound bow whose normalized force rises from 0.20 at the start of the power stroke to 1.0 at full draw. Full draw takes 2.5 seconds and exact continuous draw fraction feeds RK4 ballistics.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.4 heavy-bow playtest is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.4 build uses a 2.5-second work-based increasing-resistance draw, 50/75/100 pulse markers, continuous RK4 release strength, and no staged bow visual.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.4 validation passed
rows.statement: The heavy-bow revision passes 269/269 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.4 as PID 21484.

rows.title: Hunting windage is visible and physically coupled
rows.statement: Hunting v0.3.5 keeps crosswind inside the RK4 air-relative drag calculation and displays an in-range arrow pointing in the wind-push direction with mph. Shot results report drift direction and magnitude.

rows.title: Hunting reticle has no automatic sway
rows.statement: Live Hunting reticle movement is mouse-only in v0.3.5. Automatic sinusoidal/fatigue sway is removed from the runtime because it caused vertigo-like discomfort without adding useful gameplay.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.5 windage/stable-reticle playtest is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.5 build displays wind push direction and mph inside the shooting range, reports signed lateral drift after shots, and makes reticle motion mouse-only while preserving RK4 wind physics and v0.3.4 draw markers.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.5 validation passed
rows.statement: The windage/stable-reticle revision passes 270/270 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.5 as PID 13684.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.6 uses a strongly back-loaded smooth draw curve
rows.statement: The draw target is approximately 50% at 0.46s, 75% at 1.47s, 90% at 2.74s, 95% at 3.32s, and 100% at 4.00s. The curve is continuous and smooth rather than piecewise stepped.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.6 back-loaded draw gradient is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.6 build reaches approximately 50% draw at 0.46s, 75% at 1.47s, 90% at 2.74s, 95% at 3.32s, and 100% at 4.00s using a smooth continuous back-loaded curve and bounded inverse mapping.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.6 validation passed
rows.statement: The draw-gradient revision passes 270/270 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.6 as PID 19108.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.7 quarry movement creates timed shooting windows
rows.statement: Whitetail quarry alternates smooth horizontal walking with short stationary pauses. The long draw can be started in anticipation of a pause, making timing part of the hunt.

rows.title: Moving Hunting shots require lead
rows.statement: Hunting computes quarry position at arrow arrival time and applies its lateral displacement before anatomical hit classification. A walking target therefore requires lead; a paused target does not.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.7 moving-quarry playtest is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.7 build animates deterministic whitetail walks and stationary pause windows. Arrow-arrival quarry displacement is converted to physical lateral movement before hit classification, so moving shots require lead.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.7 validation passed
rows.statement: The moving-quarry revision passes 273/273 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.7 as PID 23564.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.8 adds visible stamina pressure
rows.statement: The Hunt window gains a Stamina gauge. Drawing drains stamina continuously according to draw strength, with greater cost near/full draw; lowering the bow recovers stamina.

rows.title: Hunting exhaustion lowers the bow instead of firing
rows.statement: If stamina reaches zero while drawing or holding, Hunting automatically lowers/cancels the draw. Exhaustion does not fire the arrow and does not apply hidden accuracy penalties.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.8 stamina playtest is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.8 build adds a visible Stamina gauge. Drawing drains stamina as 1 + 16*strength^2 per second, full draw leaves about 56 stamina from fresh, full-draw holding then lasts about 3.2 seconds, and lowering recovers after a 0.6s delay at 24 stamina per second.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.8 validation passed
rows.statement: The stamina revision passes 275/275 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.8 as PID 19700.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.9 makes arrow velocity strongly draw-sensitive
rows.statement: Launch velocity uses v = 5 + (74.5 - 5) * strength^2, producing about 22.4 m/s at 50%, 44.1 m/s at 75%, 61.3 m/s at 90%, and 74.5 m/s at full draw.

rows.title: Draw-sensitive flight time drives moving-target lead
rows.statement: Hunting moving-quarry displacement continues to use RK4 arrow flight time, so partial-draw shots travel longer and require more lead while full-draw shots minimize target movement before impact.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.9 draw-sensitive arrow speed is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.9 build uses a 5 m/s minimum and quadratic draw-strength velocity scaling while retaining 74.5 m/s at full draw. At 35 yd, 50% draw is about 1.49 s flight while full draw is about 0.45 s; at 65 yd, about 2.87 s versus 0.86 s.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.9 validation passed
rows.statement: The arrow-speed revision passes 277/277 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.9 as PID 4816.

rows.title: Hunting derives arrow velocity from stored bow energy
rows.statement: For the accepted draw curve T(s)=0.12*s+0.88*s^4, constant player pulling power makes normalized elapsed draw time proportional to accumulated bow work. Hunting uses E/E_full=T(s) and v/v_full=sqrt(E/E_full), preserving 74.5 m/s at full draw.

rows.title: Hunting reports launch speed in fps while simulating in SI
rows.statement: The engine retains meters/seconds for RK4 ballistics and converts launch speed to feet/second for the player-facing shot result.

rows.title: Future real-world draw timing must drive energy-derived arrow speed
rows.statement: If the playtest draw timing is later replaced by measured real-world bow timing, calibrate the force-draw/time curve first and continue deriving launch velocity from v/v_full = sqrt(E/E_full). Do not hand-tune partial-draw arrow speed separately. Full-draw velocity remains its own calibration unless better chronograph evidence replaces it.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.11 uses an approximately linear warbow force curve
rows.statement: The heavy self-bow approximation uses normalized draw force F/F_full=s, stored energy E/E_full=s^2, and constant-power normalized draw time T(s)=s^2.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.11 full draw target is 2.5 seconds
rows.statement: The realistic-warbow playtest targets 0.625s at 50%, 1.406s at 75%, 2.025s at 90%, 2.256s at 95%, and 2.500s at full draw.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.11 realistic-warbow model is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.11 build uses T(s)=s^2 with a 2.5-second full draw, linear force fraction, stored-energy fraction s^2, and energy-derived launch speed. Full-draw speed remains 74.5 m/s / about 244 fps.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.11 stamina consequence is documented
rows.statement: With stamina constants unchanged, the 2.5-second realistic draw leaves about 77.4 stamina from fresh and roughly 4.55 seconds of full-draw hold before exhaustion.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.11 validation passed
rows.statement: The realistic-warbow revision passes 277/277 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.11 as PID 10508.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.12 uses one synchronized flight clock
rows.statement: Arrow animation, quarry movement, and impact resolution use the same real RK4 flight duration. Visual flight is no longer capped at 1.1 seconds or used to fast-forward quarry motion.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.12 exposes movement-only dynamic lead
rows.statement: A subtle lead chevron predicts future quarry center at current arrow arrival time and updates with draw strength. It excludes wind and vertical drop and disappears for paused/negligibly moving quarry.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.12 uses actual-path tracer feedback
rows.statement: A short-lived tracer trail is rendered from sampled projectile trajectory after release so players can read and learn from the shot path.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.12 synchronized flight is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.12 build animates arrow positions from sampled RK4 states for the full physical flight duration and advances quarry movement on the same real elapsed clock.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.12 lead cue and tracer are live
rows.statement: While drawing, a faint movement-only lead chevron updates from current draw-dependent arrival time; released arrows leave a short tracer from actual sampled projectile positions.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.12 validation passed
rows.statement: The synchronized-flight revision passes 279/279 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.12 as PID 13064.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.13 removes the visible lead chevron
rows.statement: The v0.3.12 predictive lead chevron is removed from live Hunting. Synchronized arrow animation and tracer feedback remain.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.13 adds conservative moving-target aim forgiveness
rows.statement: A moving-target shot may receive at most 0.12 m of horizontal deer-relative collision correction only when the quarry is moving, the player leads in the correct travel direction, the original physical classification is a miss, and the correction converts that miss into anatomical contact.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.13 moving-target forgiveness is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.13 build removes the visible lead predictor and applies at most 0.12 m of invisible horizontal correction only to correct-direction moving-target near misses. RK4 arrow/tracer rendering remains physical and unchanged.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.13 validation passed
rows.statement: The aim-forgiveness revision passes 281/281 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.13 as PID 24660.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.14 is temporarily calm-only
rows.statement: Live Hunting shots use zero wind and expose no wind HUD or wind-drift result text so gravity/drop can be calibrated independently. Dormant wind engine code remains available for later reactivation.

rows.title: Skyrim bow math is directly portable to Java
rows.statement: Public reverse-engineered Skyrim math uses ordinary scalar interpolation/multiplication and trigonometric velocity decomposition, so it translates directly to Java. Regionwright keeps its energy-derived launch and RK4 exterior ballistics because they are more physically grounded.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.15 uses a stronger heavy-bow stamina gradient
rows.statement: Stamina drain remains effort-weighted but uses 1 + 23*s^2 points/s, reaching 24/s at full draw. With the 2.5s quadratic draw timing, a fresh full draw leaves about 68.75 stamina and about 2.86s of full-draw hold.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.15 stamina and draw pulses communicate negative vs positive state
rows.statement: Below 50% stamina the meter pulses red with a continuously shortening period toward depletion, while draw milestone pulses/reached markers use success green. Reduced-motion preference disables pulse animation.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.15 heavy-bow stamina feel is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.15 build keeps calm-only drop calibration, raises full-draw stamina drain to 24/s, pulses stamina red faster below 50%, and uses green 50/75/100 draw milestone pulses.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.15 validation passed
rows.statement: The stamina-feel/calm-only revision passes 282/282 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.15 as PID 26080.

rows.title: Future Hunting character scaling separates actor ability from bow physics
rows.statement: After neutral calibration, Dexterity will affect how quickly/effectively the character reaches draw states, while Constitution will affect stamina capacity, hold endurance, and recovery. Bow force-draw, stored energy, and projectile physics remain properties of the bow/system rather than the actor.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.16 Ballistics Lab isolates vertical calibration
rows.statement: The GM-only lab uses stationary targets and zero wind to compare Current Hybrid, Meyer Reference, and Heavy Warbow Reference profiles at fixed ranges/draw strengths without movement, stamina, actor stats, or aim forgiveness confounds.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.16 separates raw fall from sighted error
rows.statement: The lab reports raw horizontal-launch fall independently from point-of-aim error after aiming/sight elevation and verifies the physical error against its screen-pixel projection.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.16 uses one canonical projectile simulation result
rows.statement: Impact math, sampled trajectory data, and Ballistics Lab diagnostics derive from one projectile simulation result so visual and numerical projectile behavior cannot diverge by using separate formulas.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.16 Ballistics Lab is live
rows.statement: The live v0.3.16 build exposes a GM-only deterministic Ballistics Lab with Current Hybrid, Meyer, and Heavy Warbow profiles; Traditional, Pin, and Explicit Zero aiming; trajectory plotting; raw fall; point-of-aim error; physical-to-screen projection; and copied diagnostics.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.16 projectile simulation is unified
rows.statement: Impact-only and sampled trajectory consumers now share one canonical simulateArrowShot RK4 implementation, and the pre-existing live Hunting regression suite remained green after the refactor.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.16 validation passed
rows.statement: The Ballistics Lab revision passes 290/290 Regionwright tests, source/dist and installed hashes agree across 8 files, and regionwright-testmap serves v0.3.16 as PID 11700.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.19 uses canvas for Ballistics Lab plotting

rows.title: Trained Holdover is a skilled aiming solution, not a sight
rows.statement: The Ballistics Lab Trained Holdover mode represents an expert archer applying learned range compensation without a mechanical pin sight.

rows.title: Trained Holdover solves elevation against actual shot speed
rows.statement: For the selected profile, range, and draw strength, Trained Holdover solves the launch elevation needed to cross the point of aim at that range using the actual draw-dependent launch speed.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.20 Trained Holdover is live
rows.statement: The deployed Ballistics Lab offers Horizontal Reference, Trained Holdover, Automatic Pin Sight, and Explicit Fixed Zero; Trained Holdover solves elevation at the selected range using the actual draw-dependent launch speed.

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.20 validation passed

rows.title: Live holdover preserves the real Hunt systems

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.21 live holdover calibration is deployed

rows.title: Impact visual synchronization must not alter hit physics

rows.title: Hunting v0.3.25 endpoint convergence is regression-tested

rows.title: Foundry v14.367 RegionDocument offset is not a proven fixed teleport-coordinate contract
rows.statement: Exact no-write live tests on T2 Mouth B ephemeral target Region x3560/y1230/w300/h360: two repeats of center no offset and center with offset (+120,0)/(-120,0) all returned top-left (3650,1350), indicating offset did not alter center placement. Relative placement without offset threw Relative placement requires an offset. Two identical relative placement calls with offset (+120,0) returned top-left (3604,1452) and (3690,1232). Random no-snap returned (3579,1308) and (3774,1293). Temporary Token/Region objects were not persisted. Live RegionDocument spawnTokens(create:false) and teleportTokens independently call private getTokenDestinations, and teleportTokens uses foundry.documents.modifyBatch for create/delete, as seen in earlier exact runtime readback. Official v14 docs describe offset as relative and avoidOccupied for random snap placement; modifyBatch provides batched sequential modifications with cancellation on a failed operation, but does not inherently guarantee no Wall/puzzle Region/occupancy conflicts or authorized player consent. Frozen R1 handler still samples then separately recalculates teleport destination, cannot be promoted.

rows.problem: Campaign Continuity may be useful but not desirable at first glance, while Adventure Capsules may look better without proving repeat purchase or buyer value.

rows.title: Research Adventure Capsules competition, rights, and portability

rows.title: Validate the Adaptive Drop-In Capsule attendance wedge

rows.evidence_needed: Recent incident frequency, prep-time delta, no-canon comprehension, scheduled run, repeat intent, and actual price choice.

rows.title: Define the Adaptive Drop-In rights and portability packet
rows.problem: System-specific rules, stat blocks, assets, audio, and Foundry automation can block cross-VTT distribution or create licensing debt.
rows.next_action: Define an original/SRD-safe narrative packet, asset manifest, Foundry projection, and one read-only non-Foundry export before content production.
rows.evidence_needed: Rights matrix, attribution, asset provenance, export fixture, and compatibility boundary.

rows.title: Execute the exact live Foundry readiness probe

rows.evidence_needed: Versioned live receipt with supported, unknown, blocked, and stop-at-first-unsafe classifications.

rows.title: Run Game Night Rescue buyer-choice and message test

rows.title: Create a no-code Game Night Rescue hero prototype

rows.title: Run the DMF / Custom Item Workshop buyer test

rows.title: Run a side-by-side DMF versus Automaker complex-item trial
rows.problem: Automaker establishes a fast baseline, but DMF's claimed value is the behavior layer rather than the Item document.

rows.evidence_needed: Time-to-working-item, module settings touched, manual edits, disposable-scene pass, warning comprehension, real price, and live-session use.

rows.title: Run the Foundry Upgrade Guardian buyer and rehearsal test

rows.evidence_needed: Recent upgrade decision, caught failures, false alarms, time to confidence, willingness to upgrade, non-zero price, and pilot commitment.

rows.evidence_needed: No live-world mutation, exact version fingerprints, clone isolation, disk/entitlement failure handling, smoke-test receipts, and restore verification.

rows.evidence_needed: Join success, first-action time, bandwidth/device resource use, feature comprehension, setup friction, recurrence, GM purchase choice, and cross-VTT demand.

rows.evidence_needed: Join success, first useful action, battery/bandwidth use, setup time, automation fidelity, table distraction, repeat use, and actual price choice.

rows.title: Build an exact Foundry thin-client feasibility fixture

rows.title: Run Monster Field Guide qualified-GM buyer and price trial

rows.symptom: Campaign Continuity was made more visual with Canon & Branch Board.

rows.symptom: The exact target runtime was missing or only hypothetical.

rows.correction: Configure the intended Regions through Regionwright Mining with canonical ore IDs and five attempts, then add five later user-drawn nodes the same way.
rows.evidence_status: Later exact-world snapshot contains 24 configured mining deposits.

rows.symptom: Outer Travel Hub Region placements were visibly shifted relative to the map.
rows.attempted_approach: Apply a broad grid-scale correction while the hub padding was 0.
rows.failure_cause: The hub Regions were authored against the original 0.25 padded canvas, so removing padding changed their apparent alignment.
rows.correction: Restore hub padding to 0.25 while keeping width 1448, height 1086, grid size 64, and Region geometry unchanged.
rows.evidence_status: Later exact-world snapshot matches the corrected alignment state.

rows.symptom: Mining Athletics rolls and extraction summaries were visible to the table.
rows.attempted_approach: Use the default D&D5e skill roll and public ChatMessage summary.
rows.failure_cause: Default roll/message behavior exposed mining results beyond the triggering player.
rows.correction: Patch installed mining v0.1.4 to use selfroll and whisper the summary to the triggering user; provide a temporary client-local workaround until restart.
rows.evidence_status: Static source and syntax checks pass; post-restart player certification remains open.

rows.symptom: Fishing/mining Regions could be visually suppressed but player click handling still depended on document permission.
rows.attempted_approach: Leave resource Region default ownership at NONE.
rows.failure_cause: Both Regionwright resource modules gate player click handling on Region Observer permission.
rows.correction: Raise configured fishing/mining resource Regions to default Observer while preserving explicit ownership, shapes, and configuration.
rows.evidence_status: Later exact-world snapshot shows all 24 mining and all 24 fishing Regions at default Observer permission.

rows.symptom: The first immediate relaunch after stopping the regionwright-testmap process exited and port 30000 was not listening.
rows.attempted_approach: Stop the prior Foundry PID and immediately start the same executable/world command.
rows.failure_cause: The prior Foundry data-directory lock had not yet released, so the replacement correctly refused to start with a directory-locked fatal error.
rows.correction: Reread process/port/lock state, avoid blind retry, then perform one clean relaunch only after no Foundry process/listener/lock remained.
rows.evidence_status: Clean relaunch succeeded; PID 31480 listened on port 30000 and served regionwright-mining v0.2.0.

rows.symptom: The first v0.2.2 stop command returned outcome-unknown because the persistent PowerShell relay host exited before its result frame arrived.
rows.attempted_approach: Stop the process owning port 30000 and wait for listener release.
rows.failure_cause: The stop command used a PowerShell variable name colliding with the automatic $PID variable, causing the relay session host itself to terminate while the Foundry stop state became uncertain.
rows.correction: Do not replay blindly. Reconcile actual process/listener state first, then relaunch only after confirming no listener/process remained.
rows.evidence_status: Reconciliation showed no listener on port 30000; one clean relaunch then succeeded with Foundry PID 30164 listening and serving v0.2.2.

rows.symptom: First guarded migration APPLY returned FAIL_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE on T1 installed source hash
rows.attempted_approach: Create T1 RegionBehavior with source text ending in newline and compare raw string hash
rows.failure_cause: Foundry v14 schema normalizes system.source by trimming trailing LF; code text otherwise identical. Guard detected mismatch.
rows.correction: Verify restoration to 202/112, reproduce one-byte trim in no-write synthetic model, trim source input, update frozen source hashes, rerun PREVIEW and 24/24 mocks, guarded APPLY and independent FINAL VERIFY PASS at 202/113.
rows.evidence_status: recovered_verified

rows.symptom: First APPLY dispatch rejected with page.evaluate SyntaxError Unexpected token close bracket before any Foundry document write
rows.attempted_approach: Generated nested RegionBehavior data in guarded APPLY with three closing braces in flags, excluding outer object closure
rows.failure_cause: The object literal in createEmbeddedDocuments array needed four closing braces (dicebox, world, flags, root), not three. Script was never evaluated and no mutation occurred.
rows.correction: Ran local AsyncFunction syntax checker, fixed source generator and installer one missing brace, 8/8 offline tests PASS; guarded APPLY PASS and independent FINAL VERIFY PASS, with ledger/geometry/tokens unchanged.
rows.evidence_status: recovered_verified

rows.attempted_approach: Automated string replacement of earlier M1 Macro installer to M2 changed every occurrence, including unrelated global roster scene ID
rows.failure_cause: Template transformation replaced the global roster M1 Scene ID as though it were the local target Scene and could have produced a false count baseline. No live apply occurred with that version.
rows.correction: Restore M1 Scene ID in global roster while keeping M2 destination, correct generator and both generated APPLY and FINAL VERIFY, add static AsyncFunction syntax and roster check PASS before one guarded live APPLY. Independent final verify and CL90 smoke passed.

rows.symptom: Four of eight inward-offset candidate arrival centers overlap existing RegionBehaviors despite no token or wall intersection.
rows.attempted_approach: Read-only two-grid inward arrival-center and rectangular Region overlap classification; second audit read exact overlapping sources.
rows.failure_cause: A point-position no-wall check alone misses possible TOKEN_ENTER gate and story observation side effects. Rectangular overlap is not equivalent to token footprint or full navigability.
rows.correction: Distinguish candidate geometry from accepted route authority. Explicitly identify N1 rail-power gate, N2 interpretation observer and railway notices; retain approval/footprint/canary blockers instead of calling them harmless.
rows.evidence_status: PASS_READONLY_WITH_REVIEW_NO_LIVE_CANARY

rows.symptom: Initial R1 no-write verifier reported 183 Scenes / 510 Regions / 400 behaviors and BLOCKED despite canonical smoke PASS.
rows.attempted_approach: First PREVIEW counted entire game.scenes rather than the 21 known Central Lodge Scene IDs.
